steps.content: After the searing flames burn out, a desolate wilderness unfolds before you, a scene you've never seen before. Mind still hazy, you start walking.

The riverbed is dry. The earth is cracked. The sparse huts from afar look like cracked charcoal. People scatter around in twos and threes, hanging their heads in despair like the withered grass underfoot.
The sun shines in the cloudless sky, but it only reveals a scene of desolation. Compared to DisCity, this place is even more ruined, and humans seem even more powerless here.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Harbinger rose, seen in east sky... All lives perished, with ten suns high...
Unconsciously, you begin reciting the poem Du Ruo read to you before. The words taste strangely dry and bitter in your mouth.

Where are you? Is it Yanyan and Du Ruo's hometown? Is this the present, or seven years ago? You ended up here after touching that apparition of the Sun Crow. Is the Sun Crow here too? Whose memory is this? Whose dream?
You wander past the scattered groups of people and find yourself glancing at their faces, perhaps in an attempt to recognize them.
To your surprise, the moment your gaze meets theirs, these blurry faces respond to you.

steps.speaker: Disaster Victim
steps.content: ...Great Seer?

steps.speaker: Disaster Victim
steps.content: It's the Great Seer! She's back! We're safe!
You're taken aback and recoil instinctively, but your body defies your thought and goes even closer, opening your arms.
You hear a woman's voice, as bright as the sunshine.

steps.speaker: Bright Female Voice
steps.content: Oh dear, look at you, has something been troubling you while I was away? Come and tell me all about your worries.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: Where sun sank low, came where we dwelt... I'm back.
The crowd cheers as they rush over to you, and only then does the sunlight gain warmth and color, enveloping and illuminating you.

steps.speaker: Civilian A
steps.content: Great Seer, 'bout that nightmare of a great flood I had last time, was it really a premonition? Did ya check on my hometown?

steps.speaker: Civilian A
steps.content: Goodness, I'm too worried! Our town has always been prone to disasters. Should I give more offerings? I've only managed to save up a bit of grain. That enough to stop the gods' anger?

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: No need. I did visit your hometown. The disaster has been resolved, thanks to the stories passed down through generations among your townsfolk.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: Grand scales clanking, vast bones rumbling. Ever heard of this poem and the tale behind it?

steps.speaker: Civilian A
steps.content: Ah, that legend from my childhood in the village. Take a dragon's vein as bowstring and one could become a great archer and expel evil and sickness. The poem goes back to hundreds of years ago. Ya hear that whenever a child falls ill.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: Exactly, and it's no lie. During my visit to your hometown, I learned a lot while fighting Wraith Fiends underwater.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: Dragon's vein... What a wonderful thing! It'll definitely come in handy when fighting the Sun Crow in the future. The legends from your hometown are an important piece of the myth!

steps.speaker: Civilian A
steps.content: Oh! I don't remember the details, but whatever ya say must be right!

steps.speaker: Civilian A
steps.content: That's great! It's all thanks to your knowledge. 'S long as we can defeat the Sun Crow, we'll all be safe again.
The elderly woman cries tears of joy. Following her, a frail young man comes over.

steps.speaker: Civilian B
steps.content: Great Seer, I have a favor to ask. The river in my village has dried up, and at night, monsters roam everywhere. The villagers have all left over the past two years. They told me to go with them, but I...

steps.speaker: Civilian B
steps.content: I can't leave! My great-grandfather found that piece of blessed land after half a lifetime's search. It's been passed down through four generations. I can't abandon it!

steps.speaker: Civilian B
steps.content: Could ya perform a ritual to expel the evil? I don't want to leave, even if it means dying on my own land.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: I see. Even in the face of a disaster, you're still attached to your homeland and wish to respect your ancestors... I'm touched by the sincerity of your emotions. I will certainly lend you a hand.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: Blessed land is always protected by immortals. The changes now could be due to some issues with the guardian spirit. Let me seek out that immortal through divination and look into the matter...
The Great Seer begins gesturing with her fingers. Soon, she falls into a daze and starts muttering to herself.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: ...Hm? Where am I? These don't look like your fields. Have I lost my way? Could this immortal be... Ahhh!
The Great Seer's eyes are still closed, but her body jolts suddenly, then begins twitching unnaturally.

steps.speaker: Civilian B
steps.content: Oh my! Is a deity possessing ya? May, may I ask, which divine being are ya?

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: Nonsense! Divine being? Don't ya recognize me no more? I'm your great-grandfather, speaking to ya through this lass.
She jumps up all of a sudden, her face taking on a terrifying expression, and she yells...

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: My child! Listen to me with your ears perked! Just... how could ya be so dumb?! Is a piece of land more important than your life? I didn't find this land for ya to just sit around waiting to die!

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: I've already scouted it out for ya. 1500 miles to the southeast is Goldionville, where the climate is mild and the seasons are distinct. Take your family and neighbors and leave before the disaster strikes. Remember, home is where the people are. Ya got it?

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: Also! Stop calling her Great Seer. You should call her Miss Great Seer! The lass's younger than ya by a few years. Be a gentleman! ...Oh, my time here is over. Off I go!
The "possessed" Great Seer blurts out before her eyes roll back, her body falling backward. The next second, her gaze is normal again, looking somewhat stunned.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: ...Eh? What happened? I was in a trance for a while, and I saw an old man who looked just like you. He said he wanted to borrow my voice. Did he say anything to you?

steps.speaker: Civilian B
steps.content: Sob... That was my great-grandfather! I remember now. He used to talk to me like that when I was a child... Great-grandpa told me to take refuge in the south. I, I'm going to move right away. I must try my best to survive.

steps.speaker: Civilian B
steps.content: Thank you, Great... Miss Great Seer! Thank you, Sun Crow! I'll never forget your great kindness!

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: You're right, you should thank the Sun Crow, your ancestors, and yourself. Me, I am merely a messenger.

steps.speaker: Young Scholar
steps.content: You're spreading lies, smooth talker.
In the empty space behind the altar, a young scholar crosses her arms and stares at the Great Seer who is taking a break.

steps.speaker: Young Scholar
steps.content: You speak of no true oracles. You're just swindling everyone using the name of the Sun Crow. Even your so-called search for divine truths is nothing but nonsense.

steps.speaker: Young Scholar
steps.content: It's one thing for the people to be superstitious, but as Sunsink City's official seer and the one appointed to fight the disasters, how can you not clarify the truth and even play along with those fabricated stories? Have you no shame?

steps.speaker: Young Scholar
steps.content: ...No comment? I dare you to tell me your fake myth again. I will expose all of your lies.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: Well, I have nothing to add because everything you said is right!

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: Of course, I'm not smart enough to fool everyone. I'm simply taking inspiration from the people and giving back to them. After all, myths are a collective creation of the masses over thousands of years. I'm just doing a bit of consolidation and retelling them to make them relevant and practical in our times.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: You see, last time during the drought, everyone was too scared to even leave their homes. But once I wove my advice into the legends and performed a ritual, everyone had the courage to step outside and get to work. It surely solved many problems. Pretty cool, right?
Without disturbing her elegant air, the young scholar rolls her eyes.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: Don't use reassuring the public as an excuse. In the face of disasters, the real solution can only be found by confronting reality. Yet, you're depriving the people of the courage to face the truth.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: Your psychic power is strong. You're the closest to the essence of the Sun Crow and the truth of the disasters, yet you only present these lies to the masses...

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: The truth, huh... The truth is a blazing fire, a sharp knife. Only heroes dare to confront it directly, but not everyone is as brave as you. The world is mostly made up of ordinary people.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: But the choices of ordinary people... can be powerful too.
Someone comes laughing and jumping. You hear a faintly familiar laugh.

steps.speaker: Yanyan
steps.content: Great Seer, Great Seer! I dreamed of the Wraith Spirit, that fiery bird! And I'm not terrified of it anymore! I realized it was a sign as soon as I woke up, so I ran to the kitchen, and sure enough, the stove was on fire!

steps.speaker: Yanyan
steps.content: Guess what? I could suddenly work magic! I was able to control the small flames! Can Yanyan become a seer too and protect Grandma?

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: Of course. You have the same power as mine, and you're so diligent and honest... You'll go places and protect more people in the future.
The suns are far hotter than the Sun Crow you saw in DisCity. Ten of them... No, even more blinding suns hang in the sky, the melting heat sweeping across the land with the Sun Crow's kin.

steps.speaker: Sealer
steps.content: The calamity has escalated. Several allied states in Eastia have been victimized by the ten suns as well and had to abandon their cities due to the extreme heat. Something major seemed to have happened in DisCity too, cutting off trade completely. We can't import Hypercubes anymore, and our reserves are...

steps.speaker: Sealer
steps.content: The Sun Crow's power has grown too strong. Our sorcery and defense equipment are all rendered useless. We're no match for it. We have no choice but to abandon the city...

steps.speaker: Sealer
steps.content: But how should we explain this to the people? Should we admit that all the apotropaic rituals have failed us? That even the myths... can't save us?

steps.speaker: Yanyan
steps.content: Sob... Why is it so angry... What did we do wrong to deserve such punishment from the Sun Crow? What can we do to appease its anger?

steps.speaker: Yanyan
steps.content: Great Seer, can't we find instructions in the myths? Are they all... fake?

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: The disaster came too suddenly, even the seers are doubting the power of sorcery, and the effectiveness of the sealing formation has weakened.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: I've found a new shelter. It's a bit small, but it will sustain us for a while. We have the knowledge to find another home where we can live in peace, no matter how far and unreachable it may be.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: Good, take everyone with you. You speak nothing but the truth, and everyone believes what you say. Their safety is in your hands now.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: ...You're not coming with us?

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: Those myths can't hold out any longer. Are you really risking your life for this? What do you plan to do this time, Xu?!
The Great Seer smiles. Having been questioned too many times before, she can easily sidestep this one with a small lie.
The people left Sunset Town, but she has stayed behind.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: I want to... tell a lie.
Finally, she is left alone.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: I am the seer of Sunset Town, who channels Wraith Spirits, all living things, and the hearts of people. My people have turned to me, demanding an answer from the world itself.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: That's why I've long foreseen it. The calamities and evil spirits are the chaotic accumulation of human emotions. The real Sun Crow may have other names, be it fear, death, vengeance, hatred...

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: Whatever it's called, I cannot defy it. I cannot communicate with it, for it's a merciless and unstoppable thing. It's the dark side of human hearts. We have no way to deny it, and thus we find no escape.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: The myths are fake. There are no gods in this world. Even I don't have the heart to keep telling those blatant lies after seeing the truth.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: ...The truth is, they come from the people themselves.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: They don't care about the truth, the insignificance of man, or the inevitable end... In the face of disasters, they simply want to live on and be happy again. What they believe in is not courage, wisdom, or the truth, but their own wishes.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: They believe there are miracles in this vast world, that they can always find another place to call home.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: They believe that there are rules that govern all things, that kindness will be rewarded while evil will be punished.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: They believe that when evil spirits are rampant, a hero will be born, and that all tales of suffering can have a hopeful ending.
To the Great Seer who can channel all things, the most precious thing in this chaotic and cruel world is this undying glimmer of hope.
This belief has given her the strength to confront reality countless times.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: Since that's the case...

She steps steadily into the inferno, her opulent ceremonial robe torn and burned by the flames. The threads meticulously sewn and passed down through generations which once offered her protection and blessings are now turning into ashes.
What a waste. Had she known earlier, she would have taken it off and left it for the next seer. The seers must all have been envious to see her dance in these beautiful clothes.

The bright daylight is blinding her eyes. She can no longer see. Her sense of pain is numbed. With the shrieking in her ears as accompaniment, she dances to the rhythm, reminiscing about the cheerful music her folks once played for her.

The heat and Mania gnaw at her body, and her skin bursts open like new wings. The Great Seer feels that if she spreads her wings, she'll finally be able to soar high in the sky, next to the cruel gods she's spent her whole life serving and defying.

She embraces the claws of Mania, just like how she's let the Sun Crow invade and disturb her mind countless times before. This time, she will embrace all her fears and despair. And in return, she will be the one to undermine the calamity.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: Oh, revered Sun Crow, I am your seer, the one who spun tales about you every day.

steps.speaker: The Great Seer
steps.content: Would you be so kind and play along with me one last time? I want everyone to believe that the lie has come true.
Before her consciousness fully fuses with the massive Mania, the Great Seer draws her sword and points it at the Sun Crow, smiling radiantly at the last moment of her life.
